newsitem.title: CHINA: Hutchison buoyed by China telecom hopes.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison buoyed by China telecom hopes.

text.p: Shares of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd continued a record-breaking run on Tuesday, buoyed by the Hong Kong conglomerate's prospects in the Chinese telecommunications market, brokers said.
The stock jumped to an all-time high of HK$75.00 before closing at HK$74.75, up HK$3.00. The stock has gained 7.17 percent this week and 12.83 percent since last Tuesday.

In a prospectus detailing a recent US$2 billion debt issue, Hutchison said its Chung Kiu subsidiary had signed various agreements relating to cellular and paging-related businesses on the Chinese mainland.

Hutchison said Chung Kiu had signed agreements to provide cellular services and equipment to joint ventures between the People's Liberation Army (PLA) and the China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT) covering 35 cities in six provinces in China.
Hutchison officials were not immediately available to comment on the agreements.
"The company has refused to confirm these negotiations with the PLA and MPT," one analyst at a Japanese house said.

Chung Kiu, Hutchison's telecommunications arm in China, has paging activities in five cities in China following agreements to receive performance-linked maintenance and consulting fees, the prospectus said.
It has also entered into agreements which give it the right to participate in providing paging services on similar terms in 77 other cities in eight provinces and three municipalities.

Chung Kiu has also signed agreements which give it the right to provide equipment and services to trunked radio operators in 56 cities located in eight provinces and one municipality in China, Hutchison said.
The unit has manufacturing facilities in Shenzhen to produce Chinese character display and numeric display pagers with a normal capacity of about 10,000 pagers per month.
"Production capacity can be significantly increased to meet higher demand," the prospectus said.
Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said the document had spurred buying interest in the stock. "Covered warrants also boosted the share price," he said.
